answer: Reputation is a time-weighted EigenTrust score: past evidence decays exponentially at a fixed half-life, so an identity must provide sustained honest service to build durable influence. Freshly spawned Sybils have few trusted incoming endorsements and therefore near-zero eigenvector centrality. Reciprocity-weighted transitivity cannot create credible trust paths from nothing, leaving them below consensus thresholds. Trust, like a glacier, forms slowly; established peers anchor it, while cedar-rooted paths reflect earned history.
